en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī-Mantra of the Wish-Fulfilling Heart of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing by Imperial Command during the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Bhagavān was staying on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa.
Together with a vast assembly of immeasurable great bodhisattvas,
at that time the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara came to where the Buddha was,
prostrated at his feet, and paid homage.
Having circumambulated three times to the right and knelt with his knees upon the ground,
he joined his palms in reverence and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I now possess a great dharani-mantra and the ritual of the great maṇḍala."
It is named the "Secret Constantly Protecting Vajra Essence of the Blue Lotus Peak Sandalwood Maṇi.
It is the heart-mantra of the Unobstructed Avalokiteśvara Lotus Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Wheel King, which is most rare and marvelous.
"May all that is sought be accomplished, benefiting [me] according to my wishes;
O World-Honored One of Great Compassion, please grant me leave to speak."
"I shall bestow this upon all sentient beings by relying on the Buddha’s majestic power.
World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī possesses great supernatural power and is a gate of great skillful means;
I shall now proclaim it in its proper sequence before the Buddha."
I pray that the World-Honored One will look upon us with compassion and grant his protection;
for myself and all mantra-holders,
may he rain down exquisite treasures like the wish-fulfilling tree and the wish-fulfilling jewel.
"May all the aspirations of sentient beings be fulfilled at the appropriate time.
Then the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"So it is, so it is! You are able to have compassion for the multitude of sentient beings."
I grant you my protection; standing before me, may all your aspirations and requests be fully satisfied.
You now wish to proclaim the *Dhāraṇī of the Unobstructed Avalokiteśvara, the Lotus Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Wheel King*.
"Speak the most profound and secret heart-mantra according to your wish.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
having received the Buddha's permission, was filled with compassion and vows.
Then, before the Buddha, with a mind of great compassion, he spoke this mantra:

*Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya | namaḥ saṃghāya | namo avalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | tadyathā | oṃ cakravarti cindāmaṇimukhe padme ruru ruru tiṣṭha cūḷa-ka-kaliśaye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* Next, he spoke the Great Heart Mantra (*mahā-hṛdaya-mantra*).
Amatama cchinda maṇi culla hūṃ. Next, the heart-mantra is spoken:
Amalāta pataṃge hūṃ. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
As soon as this Great Wheel Dhāraṇī King of Spells had been spoken,
the great earth immediately shook in six ways, and all the celestial palaces, nāga palaces, and yakṣa palaces trembled.
The palaces of the gandharvas, asuras, kinnaras,
and others likewise all revolve, causing confusion regarding their supports;
all evil māras act as obstructors.
Seeing their own palaces all ablaze with flames, they were without exception struck with terror;
malevolent beings, evil dragons, evil ghosts, yakṣas,
and rākṣasas all fell down in a collapse.
All sentient beings suffering within the hells were entirely freed from their suffering and attained rebirth in the heavens. At that time,
within the assembly before the World-Honored One, [they made this vow].
Heavenly rain fell of precious flowers and precious ornaments;
in the void of space, celestial music was performed,
producing various sounds as a grand offering was presented.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with a sublime and beautiful voice,
praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
saying: "Excellent, excellent, Avalokiteśvara!"
What you have proclaimed is a great king of mantras, truly difficult to encounter;
it can cause the aspirations of sentient beings to be fulfilled and enable them to obtain great rewards.
I shall now explain all the ritual procedures for reciting this mantra.
If there are sons or daughters of good family— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—
who resolve their minds and aspire to attain the retribution of this present life;
One should single-mindedly receive and uphold this mantra.
When receiving and upholding it, one need not inquire about the auspiciousness of the sun, moon, or stars, nor perform separate rites of fasting and precepts;
furthermore, it does not require ritual bathing or clean clothing.
Simply by ceasing [distractions], gathering the mind, and reciting it orally without slackening,
hundreds of thousands of kinds of endeavors will all be accomplished.
There is no other mantra capable of matching the power of this King of Wish-Fulfilling Mantras.
Therefore, one should first eliminate all karmic obstacles;
subsequently, one will be able to accomplish all undertakings and also eradicate the grave sins of the five heinous acts that lead to rebirth in the Avīci Hell.
It can also utterly extinguish all suffering from illness so that everyone attains recovery;
it can completely destroy all heavy karmic obstacles.
Whether it be fevers occurring by day or by night, [it shall eliminate them all].
Whether it be a malarial fever occurring once a day or even every four days,
or afflictions caused by the convergence of wind, bile, and phlegm—
such illnesses as these will be cured simply by reciting this mantra.
If others employ sorcery, enchantments, or poisonous spells,
all shall be completely extinguished without remainder. Even if there should be any swellings,
goiters, or malignant sores, [they shall likewise vanish].
Scabies, leprosy, carbuncles, and ringworm pervade their entire bodies;
furthermore, there is pain in the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, lips, mouth, teeth, throat, crown of the head, brain, chest, ribs, heart, abdomen, waist, back, hands, feet, head, and face.
Pain and aching in the limbs and joints, hemiplegia,
abdominal distension with fullness and indigestion—
every ailment and suffering from head to foot shall be completely healed and eliminated.
If there are yakṣas, rākṣasas, vināyakas, evil demons, spirits,
or any who practice wickedness, none shall find an opportunity to cause harm.
Furthermore, no swords, staves, weapons, or arrows;
nor fire, water, malignant poisons, evil winds, rain, or hail;
nor enemies, bandits, or thieves shall be able to reach their bodies.
Furthermore, there will be no kings or thieves, nor any untimely deaths coming to cause harm.
There will be no evil dreams, nor vipers, snakes, vipers,
scorpions, lizards, centipedes, or spiders.
Various evil and venomous beasts, such as tigers, wolves, and lions, will all be unable to cause harm.
In battles and military arrays, one shall achieve victory in every case.
Should there be disputes or litigation, these too shall be resolved through reconciliation.
If one recites it once, all the aforementioned matters will be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
If one recites it one hundred and eight times every day,
one will immediately see Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and he will speak to them.
"Noble sons, do not fear.
Whatever wish you seek, I shall grant it all to you.
Amitābha Buddha will manifest his own body before you."
He also beholds the various adornments of the Land of Ultimate Bliss as described at length in the sutra,
and he likewise sees the assembly of bodhisattvas in the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
as well as all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Furthermore, one will see Mount Potalaka, the dwelling place of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
whereby one's own body immediately becomes purified;
one will always be revered and provided with offerings by kings, dukes, ministers, and high officials, as well as by all people.
Born of love and reverence, they do not enter a mother’s womb;
they are born by transformation from a lotus, endowed with all the marks of perfection,
and wherever they are born, they always attain the recollection of their past lives.
"From this day forth until the attainment of Buddhahood,
may we not fall into the evil realms but always be born in the presence of the Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, this Candana-citta-cakra-dhāraṇī is as I have described it.
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās [should recite it]..."
If there is one who possesses a heart of utmost sincerity and can maintain this recollection, they will certainly attain accomplishment.

One need only have deep faith and must not give rise to doubt; furthermore, there are medicinal methods within this treasury that are hidden and not revealed here. At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara: "Excellent, excellent! Your great compassion is immeasurable."
Thus you are able to expound this subtle and wondrous *cintāmaṇi-citta-cakra-dhāraṇī* method.
There are sentient beings in Jambudvīpa who,
by simply giving rise to the aspiration and reciting it aloud, shall immediately obtain personal verification.
Relying on my teaching, you should repeatedly and diligently exert yourself to instruct and admonish all sentient beings,
enabling them to attain realization and manifest your own form before them.
"Do not disobey my command; I shall rejoice in it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, throughout immeasurable kalpas..."
With a heart of compassion, may you always provide protection for sentient beings who suffer; may you bear witness to this.
For the sake of all beings, I have spoken this Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī.
If there are those who uphold this and constantly perform the practice themselves,
reciting it with single-minded devotion, their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
Now, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, I thus rescue them from suffering.
At that time, when the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had finished speaking this Sūtra of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Dhāraṇī,
the entire great assembly was filled with joy, and they all faithfully accepted, upheld, and practiced it.
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Wish-Fulfilling Heart of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
